identity.title: DistiLLM-2: A Contrastive Approach Boosts the Distillation of LLMs

problem.claim: Improve student-model performance in LLM distillation across varied teacher- and student-generated data.

gap.claim: Prior work generally applies identical losses to teacher- and student-generated data, overlooking interactions between loss formulation and data type.

contributions.claim: DistiLLM-2 uses a contrastive objective that increases the likelihood of teacher responses while decreasing that of student responses.
The approach is presented for instruction following, code generation, preference alignment, and vision-language extensions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors propose a contrastive distillation approach that explicitly harnesses synergy between loss formulations and data types.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments produced high-performing student models across instruction-following and code-generation tasks.
The authors report support for preference-alignment and vision-language applications.
The authors state that the findings indicate potential for improving distillation by aligning teacher and student models across varied data types.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract identifies identical treatment of teacher- and student-generated data as common in prior distillation work.
It attributes suboptimal student performance gains to ignoring the interaction between loss formulations and data types.
It introduces DistiLLM-2, which contrasts teacher and student responses through opposing likelihood objectives.
The authors report results spanning instruction following, code generation, preference alignment, and vision-language extensions.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links distinct data types with distinct loss behavior and implements this through opposing teacher- and student-response likelihood objectives.

lessons.interpretation: A paper can make its central design rationale concrete by mapping a diagnosed data–objective interaction directly to the training rule.
lessons.application: When proposing a distillation method, explicitly state which data types receive which objective terms and connect each term to the failure mode it is meant to address.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the method uses a single homogeneous data source or when objective differences cannot be justified by data provenance.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative results, baselines, task-by-task conditions, or ablations isolating the contrastive objective from other factors.
It does not specify how the method is adapted for preference alignment or vision-language extensions.
